cases.summary: Enabling `DestinationPropagation` by default replaces the removed, unsound `RenameReturnPlace` pass. The reusable correctness lesson is that renaming a local copied to the return place is invalid if that local is written again after the copy: those post-copy writes would start clobbering `_0`. A correct destination-propagation implementation must preserve the value assigned to the destination and must not treat borrowed locals as freely renameable. The retained `nrvo_miscompile_111005` test name/comment alone does not prove the replacement pass is wrong; the decoded assignments show the old pass corrupting the return value, while the replacement preserves it.
cases.trigger: A local is copied into the return place, and then that same source local is assigned a new value before the `Return`; or the local is borrowed. `RenameReturnPlace`'s eligibility check only considered the copy reaching `Return`, so it missed the later write and renamed it to `_0`.
cases.inputs: arg = 'a' (U+0061, decimal 97)

cases.summary: DestinationPropagation can replace repeated `MaybeLiveLocals` recomputation with one saved `SparseIntervalMatrix`, provided each applied source-to-destination merge is mirrored into the destination's liveness row. This preserves the liveness conflict filter while removing the per-round dataflow cost.
cases.trigger: DestinationPropagation runs multiple rounds of candidate filtering. Instead of recomputing MaybeLiveLocals each round, liveness is computed once with `save_as_intervals` into a `SparseIntervalMatrix`; after every accepted `src` -> `dest` merge, the matrix must be updated so `dest` is live wherever `src` was live before subsequent filtering.
cases.inputs: input = 7

cases.summary: Stabilizing `c_unwind` changed the ABI-unwind classification consumed by `AbortUnwindingCalls`: on stable `panic=unwind`, plain C-family ABIs were previously over-approximated as may-unwind via a feature-gated panic-strategy check; after the PR only the ABI's `unwind` flag matters. This makes plain `extern "C"` nounwind and forces unwinds crossing it to terminate, while `extern "C-unwind"` still permits propagation. The accompanying `abi_can_unwind` workaround in `ffi_unwind_calls` is removed because the helper no longer over-approximates.
cases.trigger: A Rust function or call uses a plain C-family ABI (e.g. `extern "C"`) and an unwind attempts to cross that boundary while compiling with `panic=unwind`. Under the old feature-gated logic the boundary was treated as may-unwind, so the abort/terminate decision for the unwind edge was wrong. The same trigger with `extern "C-unwind"` must continue to allow unwinding.
cases.inputs: boundary_outcome(Config { c_unwind_abi: false, panic_unwind: true, c_unwind_feature: false }) and the four control cases in the harness: feature enabled, panic=abort, C-unwind panic=unwind, C-unwind panic=abort

cases.summary: Historical Rust PR correcting the cost model used by `cross_crate_inlinable`: `Assert` terminators were charged as calls, preventing small assert-containing leaf functions from being cross-crate-inlined. The fix treats asserts as statements and adds `TailCall` to the real-call category, improving inlining without the incremental-CGU blowup caused by genuinely call-containing functions.
cases.trigger: A cross-crate-inlining candidate has one or more `Assert` terminators in its optimized MIR but no genuine calls. Under the old classification the assert increments `calls`, so the candidate can fail the call threshold and `cross_crate_inlinable` returns false; under the corrected classification the assert costs only a statement, so the candidate qualifies and `Inline` can inline the call.
cases.inputs: terms = [Term::Assert, Term::Return]; threshold = 100

cases.summary: InstrumentCoverage must emit coverage-map column numbers as 1-based UTF-8 byte offsets, not Unicode code points, because llvm-cov slices source by bytes. Using code-point columns mangles non-ASCII source or makes llvm-cov fail; empty spans must also be expanded by whole UTF-8 character byte lengths at char boundaries.
cases.trigger: A coverage-relevant span starts after one or more multi-byte UTF-8 characters on the same line, so byte offset and code-point offset differ; and/or an empty coverage span is adjacent to a multi-byte character and gets widened.

cases.summary: Bug-fix PR enabling `ConstPropLint` to lint promoted MIR bodies. Previously the pass returned early for `body.source.promoted.is_some()`, so overflowing arithmetic inside promoted expressions (e.g. `format_args!("{}", 1 << 32)` or `&(1u8 << 8)`) escaped the arithmetic-overflow/unconditional-panic lints. Removing the promoted guard makes promoted and non-promoted forms lint consistently across no-opt, optimized, and overflow-checked builds, at the cost of duplicate diagnostics when the same operator is linted in both promoted and main MIR.
cases.trigger: An expression is const-promoted (a borrowed temporary such as `&(1u8 << 8)` or a `format_args!` argument such as `1 << 32`) and the operation overflows, shifts by at least the bit width, divides/remainders by zero, or indexes out of bounds. Before the fix, `ConstPropLint` skipped promoted bodies and emitted no diagnostic; after the fix it lints the promoted operation in both non-optimized and optimized builds.
cases.inputs: The concrete issue-117949 case: is_promoted=true, operation_overflows=true (e.g. the promoted `1 << 32` inside `format_args!` or borrowed `&(1u8 << 8)`). The remaining three boolean combinations are included to show the guard only suppresses promoted bodies.

promoted=false overflows=true diagnostics=1

cases.summary: InstrumentCoverage historically emitted coverage code regions without validating their coordinates, so a region could be improperly ordered (end < start), contain a 0 coordinate, or have the high bit set in end_col. llvm-cov treats such regions as malformed and exits fatally. The fix adds a catch-all `check_code_region` filter that discards any region failing those invariants (and debug-asserts), rather than fixing each root cause in nested-macro edge cases.
cases.trigger: A coverage-eligible function produces a CodeRegion whose (start_line,start_col) is greater than (end_line,end_col), or any coordinate is 0, or end_col has bit 31 set — commonly arising from obscure nested-macro expansions or doctest offsetting.
cases.inputs: Single harness input: file_name = "edge.rs", start_line = 10u32, start_col = 5u32, end_line = 3u32, end_col = 2u32. This region is improperly ordered because (10,5) > (3,2), while all coordinates are nonzero and end_col does not have bit 31 set.

cases.summary: Const evaluation (including the evaluation path used by ConstPropLint) must distinguish immutable-static access from mutable-global access when constants are allowed to mention statics. The historical blanket "constant accesses static" rejection is too strong for immutable statics, but simply removing it would let a const read mutable global memory or carry a final value pointing into mutable memory, breaking the as-if-inlined invariant and const-pattern/valtree soundness. The correct rule is mutability-based: allow reads of immutable statics, reject reads from mutable global memory, and have const validation recursively descend into referenced statics and reject a const value that references mutable or unvalidatable extern statics.
cases.trigger: A const initializer or const fn references or reads a `static`, especially a mutable or interior-mutable static; or a const value containing a reference is converted to a valtree or used as a match pattern. The old behavior emitted `constant accesses static`; the corrected behavior allows immutable static reads but emits `constant accesses mutable global memory` for mutable reads and validation errors for const final values referencing mutable/extern statics.
cases.inputs: Runtime mutation sets G = 100 before calling read_g(1).

cases.summary: JumpThreading wrongly threaded over `SetDiscriminant` when the assigned variant is the untagged variant of a niche encoding, because that assignment does not actually write the discriminant. The fix only processes the discriminant update after checking the enum layout: Single/Direct tag encodings always write, while Niche encodings skip threading when `variant_index == untagged_variant`. The regression tests use `custom_mir` to prove the pass leaves `switchInt` unthreaded and that runtime results stay correct.
cases.trigger: `SetDiscriminant` whose `variant_index` equals the `untagged_variant` of a niche tag encoding, with a later `Discriminant`/`switchInt` that JumpThreading wants to fold to a constant.
cases.inputs: No runtime arguments. Concrete input is the enum value E::<char>::A; the generic case is instantiated as generic::<char>().

cases.summary: JumpThreading had been treating an `Assert` terminator as if it guaranteed `cond == expected`, registering threading opportunities to the matching condition's target. That is unsound because `Assert` can be compiled away at codegen time and therefore is not a semantic assumption. The fix removes the `Assert` special case and ignores `Assert` in the TOFinder, relying instead on real `Assume` facts (a `NonDivergingIntrinsic::Assume` statement); a new custom-MIR test verifies that JumpThreading still threads through an `Assume`.
cases.trigger: While flooding/visiting a block reached as a target, the terminator is `TerminatorKind::Assert`; `cond` is a place with tracked conditions; one tracked scalar condition equals the assert's `expected` boolean. In the old code this registers a threading opportunity to `c.target`. For the retained positive behavior, the block instead contains an `Assume` statement on a boolean that is subsequently used in a `switchInt`.

cases.summary: A match-lowering bug-fix PR made binding order consistent by lowering deepest bindings first, while keeping bindings at the same depth in source order. Previously refutable patterns kept bindings left-to-right whereas irrefutable patterns used a different dance, causing `x @ Pat { field }` to bind the outer value before nested fields and produce erroneous borrow-check errors. The source-backed invariant is deepest-first, same-depth source order. MIR-opt tests for EarlyOtherwiseBranch were updated because the corrected lowering reorders StorageLive/assignment pairs in their input MIR.
cases.trigger: Triggering conditions are match lowering of a candidate containing an `@` binding whose subpattern also contains bindings, especially when the pattern is refutable (under a test, e.g. an enum variant or an or-pattern) and the value/field is non-Copy. The historical inconsistency is described in the PR: "This leads to inconsistencies, as reported in https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/120210". The motivating example is `let y @ NonCopyStruct { copy_field: z } = x;`, where the field must be copied before `y` moves `x` because "the `y @` binding will move out of `x`, so we need to copy the field first."
cases.inputs: refutable = true, original bindings = [10] (outer `x`), newly discovered bindings = [20, 30] (nested `a`, `c`)

cases.summary: When `StateTransform` builds a coroutine drop shim, the shim is a synthetic non-coroutine body even though it is cloned from a coroutine. Dropping only `arg_count` without clearing `body.coroutine` leaves stale coroutine metadata, causing coroutine helper queries to misclassify the shim. The fix removes `body.coroutine` with `take()` before adjusting the argument count.

cases.summary: Decouple coverage counter-increment injection sites from BCB node/edge counter associations. Counter IDs are allocated by pushing a CounterIncrementSite (Node{bcb} or Edge{from_bcb,to_bcb}) into an IndexVec, and MIR injection iterates that site list rather than iterating per-BCB node/edge maps. This allows two coverage-graph nodes/edges to share a counter without emitting duplicate CounterIncrement statements; expression-used statements are handled separately and only for BCB nodes with coverage spans.
cases.trigger: Triggered when counter allocation assigns the same coverage counter to two or more BCB nodes/edges, or when an implementation ties MIR injection directly to per-BCB counter map entries instead of unique increment sites. Also relevant when changing edge-counter storage/iteration, because iteration order can affect emitted MIR/query stability.

cases.summary: Coverage instrumentation was computing closure body spans by unconditionally unexpanding to the outer macro call site, which lost the closure declaration context for closures declared inside macro expansions. The fix unexpands only to an ancestor in the same syntax context as the closure declaration, and separately hoists async-function span handling so the trivial desugared outer async body skips normal span refinement. `fn_sig_span` was also made optional because closures may have no usable signature span.

Also triggered when instrumenting an async function whose outer desugared wrapper spans would otherwise be refined into coverage mappings.

cases.summary: The PR moves the `cfg!(debug_assertions)` decision for `assert_unsafe_precondition!` from macro-expansion time to a new MIR `NullOp::DebugAssertions`: `LowerIntrinsics` lowers the new `debug_assertions()` intrinsic to that NullOp, `ConstPropLint` and `GVN` deliberately refuse to fold it before monomorphization, and codegen materializes `sess.opts.debug_assertions` as a bool. The same PR also teaches `InstSimplify` to mark calls to `#[rustc_nounwind]` functions as `UnwindAction::Unreachable`, admits the new NullOp in `PromoteTemps`, and adjusts `Inline` tests because the new `#[inline(never)]` precondition-check functions change inlining.

The `InstSimplify` part triggers on any MIR `Call` to a `#[rustc_nounwind]` function, closure, or coroutine whose ABI cannot unwind.

cases.summary: The PR extends MatchBranchSimplification with a new SimplifyToExp strategy: when a SwitchInt over an enum discriminant has between 2 and 64 distinct targets, all targets share the same terminator, the otherwise target is empty-unreachable, and every arm assigns the value equal to its discriminant value (possibly after an integer cast), the switch/arm chain can be replaced by a single `_0 = <discriminant> as RetTy (IntToInt)` assignment. The reusable correctness core is the negative side of that pattern: the rewrite is only valid when each arm constant actually equals the discriminant value that selects it and when there is no reachable fallback; otherwise the pass must leave the switch intact. The PR adds `_failed` and `_fallback` tests specifically to pin those non-optimizable cases.
cases.trigger: A basic block ends in `TerminatorKind::SwitchInt` whose discriminant is `Operand::Copy`/`Operand::Move`, with 2..=64 distinct switch targets, an empty-unreachable `otherwise` block, identical terminators in every target, equal statement counts, and each non-identical statement being a constant assignment to the same place whose integer value matches the discriminant value selecting that arm. The discriminant type and the arm constant type may differ (e.g. repr(i8) enum discriminant matched to i16 constants), in which case the pass emits an `IntToInt` cast.
cases.inputs: EnumAu8::B (discriminant 2)

cases.summary: Historical PR 05116c5c..+f1fef64e..+541858ed fixes async-closure MIR/ABI handling while also removing a redundant coroutine body. Before the change, async closures tracked three `AsyncFn*` futures and generated a by-ref body plus a "by-mut" clone plus a by-move body. The PR removes `by_mut_body`, renames the shared ref future to `CallRefFuture`, caps the coroutine kind so `Fn` and `FnMut` both use the by-ref body, and reserves the by-move body for `FnOnce`. It also fixes the confirmed bug that `Fn::call` on an async closure returned a body taking the receiver by move, and adjusts the `Fn`/`FnMut` shim ABI to take a pointer receiver while returning the `FnOnce`-flavored coroutine. Knowledge is assigned to `StateTransform` because the change concerns coroutine state-transform/by-move body generation and consumption. No compiler build or execution is claimed; conclusions come from the supplied diff and MIR test expectation changes.
cases.trigger: When building or selecting MIR bodies and ABI shims for an async closure whose closure kind is `Fn`/`FnMut` versus `FnOnce`, especially when `Fn::call`/`FnMut::call_mut` returns the `FnOnce`-flavored coroutine but must still borrow the closure receiver.

The fix adds an explicit `ty::Error(_) => return,` arm so the MIR pass tolerates error-recovery types instead of calling `span_bug!`.

The pass matches that error body type and, without the fix, hits its catch-all `span_bug!`.

cases.summary: InstrumentCoverage historically retained multiple coverage spans with the same source span but different nondominating BCBs via `pending_dups`. This PR simplifies the span refiner by eagerly deduplicating same-span covspans: sort closure spans first, then reverse dominator order, then `dedup_by(span.source_equal)`, keeping only one span per identical source span (closure preferred, else most-dominated BCB). The tradeoff is dropping nondominating duplicate BCBs, which changes coverage mappings in macro/closure tests.
cases.trigger: Two or more extracted coverage spans have the same source location (`span.source_equal`) but different BCBs, particularly when one is a closure span or when the BCBs are in a dominator relation. Macro-generated closures are the demonstrated trigger in the updated `.cov-map` expectations.
cases.inputs: Three spans with identical source range (lo=10, hi=20) and non-closure BCBs 0, 1, 2, where BCB 0 dominates both 1 and 2, and BCBs 1 and 2 are incomparable.

For the Inline pass, the important effect is that these method bodies now contain a `UbChecks` switch and a `precondition_check` call, which appear in Inline/pre-codegen MIR expectations when the unchecked method is inlined. cases.summary: KnownPanicsLint must not const-propagate union aggregate fields. cases.summary: The MIR validator's TypeChecker selected the coroutine body for `gen_body` based on whether the coroutine's def_id matched the body currently being validated. During MIR inlining, the callee coroutine body has already been substituted with call-site args, so it is no longer parameterized over the coroutine's original generic args. Reusing that substituted body for a coroutine-variant projection caused substitution ICEs (expected type `T` but found `Lifetime(ReErased)` or a const). The fix separates `body` (the possibly-substituted body under validation) from `caller_body` and uses `caller_body.source.def_id()` only for the query-cycle avoidance check, falling back to `optimized_mir(def_id)` otherwise.
cases.trigger: Inlining a coroutine body that has been substituted with the arguments of the call. The validator sees a coroutine-variant projection whose coroutine def_id equals the substituted callee body's `source.def_id()`, and uses the substituted body as `gen_body`; generic-args substitution then fails because the body's parameterization no longer matches the original coroutine args.
cases.inputs: lifetime_case = [GenericArg::Type(40), GenericArg::Lifetime(0)]; const_case = [GenericArg::Type(40), GenericArg::Const(9)]

cases.summary: The ByMoveBody pass (StateTransform) generates the second, by-move coroutine body used for `FnOnce`/`AsyncFnOnce` calls of coroutine-closures (async closures). Its capture analysis was wrong: it marked inner coroutine captures as by-move based only on `tcx.closure_captures(coroutine_def_id)`, without comparing against the parent coroutine-closure's captures and without accounting for the leading synthetic argument captures. The correction skips `num_args` in the inner capture list, `zip_eq`s the remaining captures with `tcx.closure_captures(parent_def_id)`, and only forces an upvar by-move when the inner capture is by-ref while the parent capture is by-move. It also builds the by-move upvars tuple by concatenating the coroutine-closure arguments with the parent closure's upvars. This fixes #123251, where a by-ref-to-by-ref capture was wrongly rewritten and produced a coroutine type mismatch.

cases.summary: Bug fix in MIR inliner cycle avoidance: when collecting callees for `mir_inliner_callees`, calls to the `const_eval_select` intrinsic must expose the function operand in `call_args[2]` as the tracked callee, otherwise recursive user functions reached through `const_eval_select` are omitted and the inliner can hit a query cycle. cases.summary: The ByMoveBody shim in StateTransform incorrectly assumed a one-to-one, same-shape correspondence between an outer coroutine-closure's upvars and the inner coroutine's upvars. Edition-2021 precise captures can split one parent capture into multiple child captures, add projections, and renumber fields, so the old zip_eq-based remapping produced wrong places. The fix builds an explicit child→parent field remapping keyed by upvar base HIR id plus projection prefix, re-applies extra precise-capture projections, and tolerates implicit reborrow derefs.

cases.summary: Bug fix for async/coroutine closures: instead of assigning the closure-env lifetime to every by-ref child capture, zip each parent capture with its child captures and only reborrow from the parent env when the child borrows closure-owned data or is a mutable borrow. This allows immutable references captured by value to retain their original lifetime, e.g. `&'a i32` rather than `&'env i32`. The historical behavior caused unnecessary borrowck restrictions (issue #123241); the heuristic is not a soundness boundary because borrowck still validates the resulting choices.
cases.trigger: Triggered when computing `coroutine_captures_by_ref_ty` for coroutine-closures, especially when a parent capture is by-move and the child capture starts with a deref projection after the parent's projection prefix (e.g. capturing `&'a i32` by move and dereferencing it), or when a child capture is a mutable by-ref borrow. The old unconditional env-lifetime assignment made the future borrow for `'env` instead of the underlying reference lifetime.
cases.inputs: Five concrete CaptureShape cases. The differentiating input is {parent_is_by_ref:false, child_kind:ByRefImm, child_has_deref_after_parent_prefix:true, child_region:7, env_region:99}: corrected returns Ref(7), historical returns Ref(99). It reuses the async-function signature-only treatment for all functions, but must still emit a signature span (otherwise llvm-cov ignores the function) and must still extract branch/MCDC mappings. Regression tests exercise while-loop conditions (plain, negated, `&&`, `||`) and compare `.cov-map`/`.coverage` output.

cases.summary: Make `#[coverage(off)]` and `#[coverage(on)]` recursive: coverage eligibility must inherit the nearest coverage attribute from enclosing defs, modules, or impl blocks instead of checking only the function's direct attribute. The fix adds a `coverage_attr_on` query walking `opt_local_parent` and moves naked-function exclusion to an explicit `NAKED` check.

cases.summary: This PR adapts Rust's MC/DC coverage instrumentation from the LLVM 18 ABI to LLVM 19. The reusable knowledge is a set of coupled invariants: condition IDs vs. test-vector indices, byte vs. bit bitmap units, start vs. end bitmap indices, false-before-true traversal order, and span containment. It is a version-compatibility migration, not evidence that a runtime coverage bug was reproduced.

cases.summary: InstrumentCoverage originally derived "hole" spans (regions to carve out of an enclosing function's coverage spans) from MIR statements that assign closure-like aggregates. That missed non-closure nested items, so their source lines were reported as executable code of the enclosing function and inherited its execution count, producing misleading coverage (issue #126626). The fix instead extracts hole spans from HIR: a visitor records every nested item span, closure expression span, and inline const block span, filters them to spans directly visible within the function body, and feeds them to the existing hole-sorting/merging/carving stage. MIR no longer contributes holes.
cases.trigger: A function body contains a nested item or other non-closure hole candidate whose span lies within the enclosing body span. Because the old MIR-based detection only recognizes closure/coroutine aggregate assignments, the nested item's span is emitted as an enclosing-function coverage span, so lines inside the nested item show the enclosing function's count (notably when the nested function is `#[coverage(off)]` or never executed).
cases.inputs: Two identical Case inputs for both variants: (1) a closure with MirAggregate::Closure, body_contains=true, same_context=true, enclosing_count=1; (2) a nested non-closure fn with MirAggregate::None, body_contains=true, same_context=true, enclosing_count=1.

cases.summary: MatchBranchSimplification folds an integer-discriminant switchInt into a single `discriminant as T (IntToInt)` when every arm yields a constant obtainable by that cast. This PR fixes the prior unsound heuristic (#124150): the old CompareType::Discr logic mixed sign/zero extension and could rewrite `-1i8` matched to `255i16` as `discr as i16`, which actually yields `-1`. The fix replaces the flag-based comparison with a `can_cast` helper that computes the real IntToInt result (sext for i8->i16/u16, zext for u8->i16/u16, trunc for i16/u16->i8/u8) and requires it to equal the target ScalarInt before enabling the transform, then removes the unsound_mir_opts gate.
cases.trigger: `MatchBranchSimplification` sees a `switchInt` on an integer discriminant where all targets lead to identical statement structures assigning constants, and each discriminant case value cast via `IntToInt` to the target constant type equals that arm's constant. When a case value is negative/narrow or a wide value truncates, the actual IntToInt semantics determine whether the transform is valid.
cases.inputs: E::A (the -1i8 discriminant whose arm returns 255i16), plus E::B and E::C

cases.summary: JumpThreading stored known constant values as u128 ScalarInt and evaluated Eq/Ne as integer bit-pattern comparisons. Applying this to floating-point constants is unsound because IEEE float equality differs from bitwise equality: -0.0 == 0.0 despite different bit patterns, and NaN != NaN despite potentially identical patterns. The fix detects floating-point constant types and bails out of creating jump-threading conditions for those equality comparisons, leaving the original switchInt in place.
cases.trigger: JumpThreading's process_assign path encounters an Eq/Ne comparison involving a constant whose type is floating point, after the known value is about to be normalized and converted with try_to_scalar_int for integer comparison.
cases.inputs: No function arguments: x is fixed to -0.0 and compared against 0.0.

cases.summary: GVN gains `simplify_aggregate_to_copy`, rewriting an aggregate construction whose fields are a one-to-one `Field(i)` projection chain of one common base place into a single `Rvalue::Use(Operand::Copy(base_place))`. The rewrite is guarded by same-nominal-type, field-order, enum-variant, and base-not-mutated conditions, and it must mark reused locals so their `StorageLive`/`StorageDead` are removed. The PR adds MIR-opt tests for each guard (different type, swapped fields, mutated base, enum same/different variant, storage-dead/index) plus end-to-end codegen/pre-codegen tests.
cases.trigger: `simplify_aggregate` is processing a `Value::Aggregate`/`AggregateTy::Def` rvalue and every field value is a projection of one common base value, with `ProjectionElem::Field(index, _)` matching the field position one-to-one, and the reconstructed copy place has the same type as the rvalue. For enums, a `Downcast` on the source path must match the aggregate's `variant_index` (and is then stripped); a mismatched variant blocks the rewrite.
cases.inputs: SameType { a: 3, b: 8 }

cases.summary: PR fixes `ElaborateBoxDerefs` for debug var infos whose place contains a `Deref` on `Box<T>`. The old projection-rebuilding logic duplicated the original box deref, producing an invalid double-deref place such as `*(*(((_1.0).0).0))`; the corrected pass replaces the box `Deref` with the `Unique`/`NonNull`/`*const` field projections plus exactly one `Deref`, and preserves later projections once. The focused regression test is custom MIR `debug foo => *opt;` with a MIR diff, plus a run-pass async-closure test for the downstream ICE.
cases.trigger: A `VarDebugInfoContents::Place` contains a `Deref` projection on a base of type `Box<T>`, so `ElaborateBoxDerefs` must elaborate that box dereference in the debug-info place. The bug is specifically exercised by debug var infos, not by ordinary non-debuginfo places, and historically was not covered by existing tests or stage2 code.
cases.inputs: opt = Box::new(Box::new(7_i32))

cases.summary: Bug fix for MIR inlining: `Inliner::check_mir_body` now rejects callee bodies marked `tainted_by_errors` before performing the inline threshold/cost checks. Tainted error-recovery MIR is not necessarily well-formed, and inlining it could lead to ICEs such as the closure-argument tuple assertion or missing `mentioned_items`. The regression was moved from `tests/crashes/122909.rs` to a UI test under `tests/ui/polymorphization/inline-tainted-body.rs` with expected diagnostics and no ICE. This knowledge comes from the patch and linked issue text; no compiler was built or run.
cases.trigger: While compiling an already-invalid crate with MIR inlining enabled, the inliner considers a callee whose MIR body has `tainted_by_errors = Some(_)`; before the fix, `check_mir_body` does not reject it early.

The historical bug kept the first unreachable block's original span/scope, allowing debuggers to map breakpoints to the wrong instruction. The fix sets the kept terminator's SourceInfo to DUMMY_SP and OUTERMOST_SOURCE_SCOPE whenever at least one unreachable block was deduplicated.

cases.transformedOutput: dedup span=111 scope=1 single span=333 scope=7

cases.summary: Rust 1.80.1 includes a confirmed JumpThreading miscompilation fix: the pass reduced floating-point Eq/Ne comparisons to integer/bit-pattern comparisons of ScalarInts. Because float equality does not follow bit patterns (-0.0 == 0.0 although their bits differ; NaN != NaN), it could prove the wrong condition and thread control flow to the wrong branch. The fix makes process_assign bail out for floating-point constants. The same point release also reverts unrelated dead_code lint changes, but the reusable pass-level knowledge is the JumpThreading float-comparison bug.
cases.trigger: A float comparison of the form `if x == C` or `if x != C` where JumpThreading knows x's constant and processes the resulting boolean assignment. Minimal example from the regression test: `let x = if true { -0.0 } else { 1.0 }; if x == 0.0 { 0 } else { 1 }`.
cases.inputs: No arguments. The concrete value is x = -0.0 selected by `if true`; the compared constant is +0.0.

cases.summary: Historical JumpThreading bug fix: floating-point Eq/Ne comparisons must not be folded through integer ScalarInt/bit-pattern comparisons; this was the fix for issue #128243, backported as “Disable jump threading of float equality #128271”.
cases.trigger: `process_assign` sees a `BinOp::Eq` or `BinOp::Ne` with an available constant condition, maps it to `ScalarInt::TRUE` or `ScalarInt::FALSE`, and—before the fix—reaches `try_to_scalar_int()` without rejecting a floating-point constant.
cases.inputs: No runtime arguments. The fixed values are -0.0f64 compared for equality with 0.0f64, and f64::NAN compared for inequality with the same-bit-pattern constant f64::NAN.

cases.summary: EarlyOtherwiseBranch was extended from hoisting enum-discriminant computations to also folding nested scalar matches (e.g. `match (x, y) { (1,1)=>..., (2,2)=>..., (3,3)=>..., _=>... }`). For a child block with no statements whose `SwitchInt` directly tests `Operand::Copy(place)`, the pass now hoists `Ne(parent, child)` before the parent switch; for the existing discriminant case it still hoists `Rvalue::Discriminant`. Correctness depends on same-typed places, exact one-to-one matching of inner/outer switch values, `Copy` (not `Move`) for the scalar operand, and preserving the old UB guard for discriminant hoisting.
cases.trigger: A parent `SwitchInt` dispatches to child blocks that each switch on the other component of a same-typed pair with the same corresponding constants, so the two-level dispatch can be collapsed into one equality/`Ne` test plus the parent switch.

cases.summary: Historical bug fix in the `ByMoveBody` coroutine MIR pass: when the parent capture is by-ref but the child capture is by-value, the pass must insert a leading `Deref` projection to convert the parent's upvar type into the child's; otherwise the generated coroutine-kind-shim body contains a type-incorrect assignment and validation ICEs (issue #129074). The fix also replaces the old `needs_deref` condition with explicit `peel_deref` handling for child-by-ref and always validates the generated body.
cases.trigger: A coroutine-closure's parent capture is by-ref while the child coroutine's capture for the same place is by-value. The child becomes by-value specifically because the body moves a non-`Copy` value out from behind a shared reference, so parent upvar type is `&&Ty` while child upvar type is `&Ty`.
cases.inputs: payload values: 7, -3, 42

cases.summary: Confirmed unsoundness fix: HIR typeck must not insert `NeverToAny` or mark a block as diverging for a syntactic place expression of type `!` when the parent context does not actually read that place (raw addr-of, wildcard match/let, LHS assignment). The PR fixes #117288; SimplifyLocals MIR tests observe the corrected generated MIR.
cases.trigger: The expression is a syntactic place expression whose type is `!`, and its parent HIR node is `AddrOf`, `Field`, `Assign` (expression is the LHS), `Match`/`Let` (scrutinee/init where all relevant patterns are non-reading), or a `LetStmt` initializer with a non-reading pattern. In those cases the old code incorrectly inserted `NeverToAny` and/or treated the expression as diverging.
cases.inputs: input = 0x40 as *const ! (dangling pointer; the place `*input` is never read)

cases.summary: The AbortUnwindingCalls pass previously replaced a call's unwind action with `Terminate` even when it was `Cleanup`, which bypassed landing pads and prevented destructors on non-unwinding `extern "C"` frames from running. The fix preserves `Cleanup`, runs it, and only then converts the cleanup block's `UnwindResume` into `UnwindTerminate(Abi)`; it also restricts direct replacement to `UnwindAction::Continue`.
cases.trigger: The function body cannot unwind (`body_can_unwind == false`, e.g. `extern "C"`) and contains either a call that may unwind with `UnwindAction::Cleanup`, or a cleanup block whose terminator is `UnwindResume`.
cases.inputs: unwind_cleanup_model(1) models a callee that unwinds; unwind_cleanup_model(0) models a normal return. Both use deterministic integer inputs.

cases.summary: The MIR inliner's cycle-breaker search must not use the same recursion limit as the trait solver under `-Znext-solver`: doing so lets the solver overflow fatally first. The backported fix halves the inliner's recursion budget so the cycle breaker gives up on inlining rather than producing a fatal solver error.
cases.trigger: MIR inlining cycle detection (`mir_callgraph_reachable`/`process`) recursively walks a call graph while invoking trait solving, with the next trait solver enabled; each recursion level increases the type complexity handed to the solver.
cases.inputs: target_level = 200 (deep), target_level = 10 (shallow); fixed solver recursion limit = 128

cases.summary: InstrumentCoverage previously recognized only bang macro expansions when deduplicating/unexpanding coverage spans, so `await` desugaring exposed its `Poll` discriminant branch and await coverage depended on the future actually suspending and resuming. The fix generalizes `visible_macro: Option<Symbol>` to `expn_kind: Option<ExpnKind>` and deduplicates both `DesugaringKind::Await` and bang-macro spans by span, keeping the first in dominator order, while continuing to split only visible bang macros.
cases.trigger: An async function under coverage instrumentation contains an `.await` whose future completes without ever yielding; without special handling of the await desugaring, the await's coverage is not counted as expected. Conditional match expressions with multiple awaits also produce duplicate await-related span mappings that need collapsing.
cases.inputs: Covspans in dominator order: await@14, await@14 (duplicate), await@20, bang_macro@30, bang_macro@30 (duplicate), none@40, other@50. The duplicate await spans model the repeated await-related mappings seen in async::i; non-await/non-macro spans must remain untouched.

cases.summary: Confirmed bug fix in the Inline-related compiler pipeline for async closures. The synthetic by-move MIR body of a coroutine-closure's FnOnce implementation was neither recorded in `mir_keys` nor encoded/decoded through a metadata table, and `DefKind::SyntheticCoroutineBody` was omitted from function-like/inlining classifications. Consequently `optimized_mir` was not encoded for that body and the Inline infrastructure failed to ensure `mir_inliner_callees` before MIR was stolen, causing a Steal ICE under `-Zinline-mir`; cross-crate inlining also could not recognize the synthetic body. The fix makes the synthetic def-kind fn-like, adds it to cross-crate inlinability and symbol-mangling global-sharing checks, encodes `coroutine_by_move_body_def_id` in metadata, and inserts the synthetic body into `mir_keys`.
cases.trigger: An async closure is used in a context requiring its synthetic by-move body, such as calling it through `impl async FnOnce`, or when such a closure is defined in one crate and consumed in another. With `-Zinline-mir`, the Inline machinery may process the synthetic body without having ensured `mir_inliner_callees`, producing a Steal ICE; cross-crate optimization may also miss or mis-handle the body because its def-id is absent from metadata.
cases.inputs: A single DefKind value: DefKind::SyntheticCoroutineBody, representing the synthetic by-move MIR body synthesized for an async closure's FnOnce implementation.

cases.summary: Fixes semi-nondeterministic inlining of recursive/mutually-recursive local calls by deleting the inliner's `DefPathHash`-ordering early return and relying on the existing `mir_callgraph_reachable` cycle check. The old hash-based cycle breaker inlined some cycles only when caller/callee hashes happened to be ordered a certain way, making MIR output and ICE minimization unstable. This changed test expectations: `f::<fn() {g}>` is no longer inlined into `main` in the `cycle` test, and the generic cycle test no longer produces the deeper `scope 4`/`scope 5` inlined scopes.
cases.trigger: A local call in a recursive or mutually recursive call graph where the old `DefPathHash` comparison would allow inlining, for example `f(g)` where `f` is generic over a function item that can call back, or generic `Call` impls forming an A/B/C cycle. With the old code, hash ordering can cause additional `scope N (inlined ...)` scopes that disappear after removal.
cases.inputs: FAVORABLE_HASH_CYCLE=(caller_hash_lt_callee_hash=true, callee_reaches_caller=true); UNFAVORABLE_HASH_CYCLE=(false, true); ACYCLIC_CONTROL=(false, false)

cases.summary: Historical compiler PR enforces that interpreter errors raised during speculative const evaluation in DataflowConstProp, GVN, JumpThreading, and KnownPanicsLint must never be silently swallowed. The interpreter result type gains a drop guard that panics unless the error is explicitly discarded, propagated, or reported; pass sites that previously consumed InterpResult via plain `.ok()`/implicit drop now call `.discard_err()`, while combined fallible operations use `and` to make error precedence explicit.
cases.trigger: A pass consumes a failed `InterpResult` without exhausting it, e.g. `expr.ok()`, `expr.is_err()`, or letting the result fall out of scope, rather than calling `discard_err()`, using `?`, or `report_err()`. The new drop guard then panics with "an interpreter error got improperly discarded; use `discard_err()` if this is intentional".
cases.inputs: input = 0

cases.summary: Bug fix in the InstrumentCoverage query `coverage_attr_on`: malformed `#[coverage(..)]` attributes can still reach this query in builds that are already failing validation, so the unexpected-value branch must use `span_delayed_bug` instead of aborting `span_bug` to avoid an ICE. Regression coverage moved from a `tests/crashes` known-bug test to a revisioned UI test.
cases.trigger: `coverage_attr_on` encounters a `coverage` attribute whose parsed argument shape is neither exactly `on` nor the accepted off-form (for example `#[coverage]`), and this query is reached while compiling with coverage instrumentation (e.g. during `mir_built`/analysis), even though the crate is going to fail due to the malformed attribute or its feature gate.
cases.inputs: The concrete input is CoverageAttrInput::Bare, modeling the malformed bare `#[coverage]` attribute from the reproducer under -Cinstrument-coverage. The identifier is queried as if for `fn main() {}` with no enclosing coverage attribute.

cases.summary: JumpThreading's condition transfer for `Rvalue::UnaryOp(UnOp::Not, place)` inverted the polarity of the source condition as if `!` always acted as a logical not. That is valid only for `bool`; for integer operands `!` is a bitwise complement, so the pass wrongly treated `!a == b` (equivalently `(!a) == b`) as the negation of `a == b`, i.e. `a != b`. The fix guards the transfer with `place.ty(...).ty.is_bool()` and returns otherwise, leaving the condition unthreaded. The added MIR test records that `bitwise_not` keeps its `switchInt` rather than folding on the non-bool equality.
cases.trigger: The `TOFinder` matches `Rvalue::UnaryOp(UnOp::Not, Operand::Move(place) | Operand::Copy(place))` and the operand type is not `bool`; before the fix it immediately inverted and inserted the known condition rather than returning.
cases.inputs: bitwise_not(-3), bitwise_not(-2), bitwise_not(-1), bitwise_not(0), bitwise_not(1), bitwise_not(2), bitwise_not(3)

cases.summary: JumpThreading miscompiled integer `!a == b` by inverting equality polarity instead of computing the bitwise NOT of the condition value. The fix removes `Condition::inv` polarity inversion for `UnOp::Not` and evaluates `Not` on the tracked scalar constant, while making condition mapping fallible so const-eval errors discard all opportunities from that switch.
cases.trigger: A `SwitchInt` condition is traced backward through an assignment `lhs = Not(place)`, `state.try_get_idx(lhs, ...)` has conditions for `lhs`, and `self.map.find(place.as_ref())` succeeds. With the old code the Not branch inverts each condition's polarity; with the new code it applies `UnOp::Not` to each condition's `ScalarInt` value using the layout of `place`.
cases.inputs: check called with fixed integer inputs -2, -1, 0, 1, 2; no external input

The PR also replaces an HIR over-approximation with a MIR maybe-initialized drop-reachability lint to avoid false positives for consumed/moved/parameter/closure-capture values.

cases.summary: Historical bug fix in JumpThreading: polarity inversion through `UnOp::Not` is valid for logical bool negation but not for integer bitwise negation. The pass previously rewrote the condition behind `!a == b` as `a != b` for non-bool integers, changing branch behavior. The fix only performs the inversion when the not operand's type is bool, and adds a MIR-opt regression test showing the `switchInt` is retained for an `i32` case.

cases.summary: Historical PR disables GVN's `simplify_aggregate_to_copy` mir-opt (added in #128299) by gating it behind `-Zunsound-mir-opts`, because the rewrite can replace aggregate construction with `copy (*_place)` and thereby introduce aliasing-unsafe new dereferences. The regression is demonstrated with a `run-pass` UI test at opt-level 0 and 1, plus a GVN MIR-diff test showing the bad `_0 = copy (*_2)` rewrite.

cases.inputs: a is initialized to Some(7) and passed as &mut Option<i32>

cases.summary: Historical bug-fix PR marks GVN's `simplify_aggregate_to_copy` MIR optimization as unsound because it rewrites aggregate construction into a copy of an aliasing place, introducing new dereferences without aliasing checks, so a later write through an alias can change the value read. The fix gates the optimization behind `-Zunsound-mir-opts`. Reusable knowledge: when testing GVN copy/aggregate canonicalization, check that any reused aggregate value is not invalidated by intervening mutable aliasing.
cases.trigger: GVN sees an aggregate `Rvalue` (`AggregateTy::Def`) that it can canonicalize to an existing aggregate value while there exists a live alias to the place that is written between the original read and the replacement copy. In the minimized case: read `Some(col)` out of `&Option<i32>`, overwrite `*v = None`, then return `Some(col)`; GVN instead emits `copy (*_2)` after the overwrite, reading `None`.
cases.inputs: v = Some(42)

cases.summary: GVN's old two-phase value numbering computed SSA values through `for_each_assignment_mut`, which skips side-effecting statements such as dereference assignments. As a result, a value derived from an immutable-reference deref `*r` could be reused after a non-local mutation to the same memory, producing a stale read (e.g. `Some` became `None` after `*v = None`). The fix removes the pre-pass and computes values on the fly in reverse postorder, tracking interned derefs and invalidating them (turning them into `Value::Opaque`) whenever a mutating place use with a non-empty projection or an unsafe terminator (anything other than `SwitchInt`/`Goto`) is encountered.
cases.trigger: A deref projection `*r` through an immutable `&Freeze` reference is interned via `insert_deref`, then a write to a place with a non-empty projection (or an unsafe terminator) may alias the same memory, and GVN later reuses the interned deref value instead of re-reading/using the field value.
cases.inputs: v = Some(42)

cases.summary: Coverage span lowering in `InstrumentCoverage` changed empty-span expansion from a general one-character nudge to a brace-specific rule. An empty span is now expanded only to the following `{` or preceding `}`, within the function body span; otherwise it is skipped. This avoids expanding empty spans over arbitrary characters and past physical line ends. File identity for the function's mappings is now taken from `FunctionCoverageInfo::body_span`, because a function's coverage spans are currently assumed to be in one file. Focused coverage tests should compare brace-adjacent empty spans with identical spans adjacent to newline/space/non-brace bytes, plus body-boundary and Unicode cases.
cases.trigger: During coverage instrumentation, `make_source_region` receives an empty span. The historical code expands it by one character boundary in either direction; the corrected code invokes `ensure_non_empty_span` and expands only if the next source byte is `{` or the previous source byte is `}` (subject to body-span bounds).
cases.inputs: src = "if c { f(); }\n" (len 14, '}' at byte 12, '\n' at byte 13); lo = 13; hi = 13; body_lo = 0; body_hi = 14. Historical result: Some((14, 15)); corrected result: Some((13, 14)).

cases.summary: The PR moves coverage counter/expression "seen" tracking from codegen's per-instance MIR traversal into `CoverageIdsInfo` computed by the `coverage_ids_info` query. Codegen then uses those query bitsets to zero mappings, with unused functions always zeroed. This is an optimization/cleanup with intentional behavior changes for MIR-inlining/instantiation cases; it is not presented as a confirmed bug fix.
cases.trigger: A coverage counter or expression is present in a function's coverage info/MIR but is absent from the codegen traversal of a particular instantiation, for example because of MIR inlining or instantiation-specific optimization, or because the whole function is unused. The old per-instance sets then classify the ID as optimized away and rewrite it to `Zero`, whereas the query-based result is consistent across instantiations.
cases.inputs: num_counters=2, mir_counter_ids=[0,1], instance_counter_ids=[0], mapping_counter=1

cases.summary: GVN historically treated dereferences of shared references to `Freeze` pointees as reusable values, allowing a load before an opaque call to be substituted for a later load after that call. The PR marks this as unsound (issue #130853), disables it unless `-Zunsound-mir-opts` is enabled, and updates GVN/MIR and coverage expectations.
cases.trigger: A dereference through a shared reference whose pointee is `Freeze` is followed by an opaque call and another dereference/read of the same place, under GVN without the `unsound_mir_opts` guard.
cases.inputs: value = 0u8; x = &&value; unknown writes 1u8 through a raw pointer to probe's local y after the first **x load.

cases.summary: This revert restores early `SourceRegion` construction and validation in `InstrumentCoverage`, instead of storing raw `Span`s and validating each mapping later during LLVM coverage map generation. The regression was serious enough that #133418 was reverted. The historical test updates show zero-width coverage spans being expanded to adjacent braces before emission (`14:10 - 14:10` became `14:9 - 14:10`; `21:2 - 21:2` became `21:1 - 21:2`; `14:39 - 14:39` became `14:38 - 14:39`). The key MCDC invariant is also restored: emit an `MCDCDecision` only when all conditions and the decision span produced valid source regions; otherwise downgrade all conditions to ordinary `Branch` mappings.
cases.trigger: Compile a coverage-instrumented function using the `Span`-storing/deferred-validation transformation where a mapping span is empty or otherwise invalid, or where an MCDC decision has condition spans that do not all convert. The incorrect path can emit zero-width/invalid regions or leave a decision mapping while dropping individual condition mappings.
cases.inputs: conditions_valid = 0b101 (conditions 0 and 2 valid, condition 1 invalid); decision_valid = true; NUM_CONDITIONS = 3

cases.summary: In Rust's ElaborateDrops pass, lint-only "backward incompatible drop" hints were scheduled as ordinary value drops (DropKind::Value plus a backwards_incompatible_lint flag) and thus handled as normal drops in several drop-elaboration paths. That emitted real drop calls for a lint-only no-op, causing duplicate Drop::drop invocations and unsoundness. The fix introduces DropKind::ForLint and handles it specially wherever drops are built/elaborated, emitting only BackwardIncompatibleDropHint statements.
cases.trigger: A lint-only scheduled drop (originally `DropKind::Value` plus `backwards_incompatible_lint: true`) is elaborated into a real drop, especially on unwind/cleanup paths where the drop tree or `build_scope_drops` treats it like a normal value drop. The hint statement is then emitted alongside one or more actual `drop(...)` terminators for the same local. The issue reports: "I expected to see this happen: Drop is called twice." followed by "Instead, this happened: Drop is called 3 times."

cases.summary: Re-landed coverage optimization that keeps coverage regions as `Span` through MIR and defers line/column conversion to LLVM codegen. The reusable correctness lesson is that this deferred conversion can reject spans (empty/improper/zero/high-bit `end_col`), and a used function may consequently have zero regions; codegen must skip such functions instead of asserting or emitting metadata that makes `llvm-cov` abort. Regression coverage uses a testing-only `-Zcoverage-options=discard-all-spans-in-codegen` flag plus an aux crate providing valid coverage metadata.
cases.trigger: A coverage-instrumented function has mappings whose `Span`s cannot be converted to valid LLVM coordinates, or all of its spans are discarded during codegen (empty span not expandable to an adjacent `{`/`}`, zero line/column, `end_col` high bit set, or end before start). The regression trigger is explicitly forced with `-Zcoverage-options=discard-all-spans-in-codegen`, which makes codegen discard every span as though invalid.
cases.inputs: spans = [VALID_SPAN (10:1-10:11), INVALID_SPAN (0:1-10:11)], used = true, discard_all_in_codegen = true and false

cases.summary: Historical fix for drop elaboration of lint-only drops used by the Edition-2024 `tail_expr_drop_order` lint. Lint drops must be a distinct `DropKind::ForLint`, not a `Value` drop carrying a `backwards_incompatible_lint` boolean. On normal exits they emit only `BackwardIncompatibleDropHint`; on unwind paths and inside coroutines they must be handled with lint/storage semantics so the unwind drop tree does not perform a real `drop` for a lint-only local and the coroutine transform does not ICE.
cases.trigger: A `BackwardIncompatibleDropHint`/`ForLint` drop node is present at a scope exit that also has unwind cleanup, or the lint hint is emitted inside an async/coroutine body.
cases.inputs: unwind = true (cleanup/unwind path); unwind = false (normal path)

cases.summary: Adds InstSimplify::simplify_repeated_aggregate, rewriting an array aggregate of at least five identical *constant* elements (e.g. [0, 0, 0, 0, 0]) into Rvalue::Repeat ([0; 5]). The rewrite is sound only if full const-evaluation results are compared; distinct references to equal referents have different addresses and must not be collapsed. Local/move operands are intentionally not handled (GVN handles those).
cases.trigger: An array aggregate with at least five fields where every field is `Operand::Constant`, each const-evaluates successfully, and every evaluated value equals the first evaluated value.
cases.inputs: single call with unit input: repeated_refs(())

cases.summary: Rust 2024 tail-expression drop-order migration bug fix: BID hints must be scheduled for all tail temporaries, not only those with significant drop, so borrowck can detect borrows that would become invalid at the future drop location. The patch also avoids an opaque-normalization query cycle in the tail_expr_drop_order lint by using a non-body-analysis typing environment. ElaborateDrops MIR fixtures record the newly retained BID statement.
cases.trigger: A `StatementKind::BackwardIncompatibleDropHint` with `BackwardIncompatibleDropReason::Edition2024` is reached while a borrow involving the hinted place is still in scope, or the tail_expr_drop_order lint normalizes a recursive local opaque type. The hint is associated with a temporary whose drop order changes under Rust 2024, and the type may or may not need `Drop`.
cases.inputs: INPUT = [Temp{sig:true,live:true}, Temp{sig:false,live:true}, Temp{sig:true,live:false}, Temp{sig:false,live:false}]

cases.summary: Adds a tracked `-Z hint-mostly-unused` option that makes the MIR `Inline` pass treat crate-local functions as cross-crate inlinable so codegen can be deferred until callers reference them. This is a compile-time optimization, not a confirmed bug fix; the flag is explicitly a hint and is intentionally placed after the `#[inline(never)]` rejection so that rejection still wins.

cases.summary: Folding `Rvalue::Len` is valid from the place type and tracked wide-pointer metadata: use the static length for array-typed places, use tracked length only for a bare `[Deref]` slice place, and in GVN preserve length only through simple `[Deref]` reborrows and array-to-slice unsizing; otherwise retain an opaque symbolic `Len`.
cases.trigger: A statement `_l = Len(place)` in built/runtime MIR, typically introduced by indexing/bounds checks or by `mir_len` custom MIR, where `place.ty` is `Array` or `Slice`.
cases.inputs: array = [10u32, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60], lo = 1, hi = 4; expected real subslice length = 3, but source array length = 6

cases.summary: Bug-fix: dropck can fail only after HIR typeck because it inspects projected field types; borrowck must rerun dropck with diagnostics, and ElaborateDrops must use fallible normalization and only synthesize an error type when the body is already tainted by those errors. Otherwise a recoverable projection-normalization error becomes an ICE in drop elaboration.
cases.trigger: During MIR borrowck/liveness, `compute_drop_data` performs the `DropckOutlives` type-op for a local type and gets `Err`/`NoSolution`; the error is only discoverable in dropck, not HIR typeck. If borrowck swallows it, `ElaborateDrops` later calls `normalize_erasing_regions` on a field type and panics instead of emitting the expected type error.
cases.inputs: normalization_ok = true (all field types normalize) and normalization_ok = false (projection normalization fails only when dropck inspects fields). The false case is the historical dropck-only error.

cases.summary: CheckNull previously guarded every null-pointer check with a "pointee is not a ZST" test, so a null raw pointer dereferenced in a borrow context (`&*ptr` or `&mut *ptr`) to a ZST was not checked. The fix makes borrow contexts check unconditionally, while reads and raw borrows of null ZST pointees remain allowed.
cases.trigger: A MIR place read through a null raw pointer whose pointee type is zero-sized, where the place is consumed as a shared borrow (`&*ptr`) or mutable borrow (`&mut *ptr`) under `-C debug-assertions`. Plain reads of the same null ZST pointee (for example `let _ = *ptr;`) and raw borrows (`let _ = &raw const *ptr;`) are allowed and must not trigger the null check.
cases.inputs: All calls use std::ptr::null::<()>(), i.e. a null pointer to the ZST (). The four calls vary only the place-use context: SharedBorrow, MutBorrow, Read, RawBorrow.

cases.summary: A bug-fix PR completing MIR visitor coverage: `super_terminator` now visits `fn_span` for `Call` and `TailCall`, `super_local_decl` visits `source_info` before the type, and the inliner's `Integrator` visits `source_info` for `Return` terminators. This matters when inlining rewrites debug spans: incomplete visiting leaves some spans stale or unprocessed.
cases.trigger: Any MIR transformation whose visitor overrides `visit_span`/`visit_source_info` and relies on the visitor to reach all embedded spans, especially inlining of calls and handling of `Return` terminators.
cases.inputs: seed = 7 (one concrete u64; both functions construct the identical Body from it)

cases.summary: Bug fix: const-eval's `ensure_monomorphic_enough` stopped rejecting types that only contained generic parameters nested inside `FnDef`/closure/coroutine substs. A `generic::<T>` function item was therefore treated as monomorphic enough, `type_id` was evaluated with an uninstantiated `T`, and GVN folded the resulting constant comparison to a fixed boolean (reported as `false` in release). The fix reverts to throwing `TooGeneric` whenever the type has any parameter, keeping the comparison as `Eq(const ...<T>..., const ...<T>...)`; the new MIR regression test asserts that GVN does not fold it.
cases.trigger: Const eval needs to interpret `type_id` for a type that contains a generic parameter only underneath a `FnDef`/`Closure`/`Coroutine`/`CoroutineClosure` (e.g. `generic::<T>`), and then GVN sees an `Eq` of two constants derived from those evaluations.
cases.inputs: concrete instantiation T = i32, passed as 32

cases.summary: Extend the raw-pointer alignment check to borrows and make field-projection borrows check the field type, not the raw pointer's pointee type; keep the null check on the pointer rather than following projections.
cases.trigger: A shared or mutable borrow `&(*ptr)` / `&mut (*ptr)` or `&(*ptr).field` / `&mut (*ptr).field` is created from a sized raw-pointer pointee whose runtime address is misaligned under debug assertions.
cases.inputs: A 4-byte-aligned stack array [u32; 2] = [0xAAAAAAAA, 0xBBBBBBBB]; ptr = array.as_ptr().byte_add(1) so ptr % 4 == 1; stored value = 42.

cases.summary: Bug fix in `AddCallGuards`: the pass previously split critical edges only for calls, not for inline-asm terminators. Inline asm defines outputs along its fallthrough and label target edges, and codegen writes those outputs directly into each target block; if a target has other predecessors, the asm output store is emitted on the wrong path and can overwrite values assigned by a label body. The fix extends the critical-edge splitting to `InlineAsm` when the asm has outputs and either labels or an invoke unwind.
cases.trigger: An `InlineAsm` terminator with an output operand (`InOut` or `Out`) and labels and/or an unwind that generates an invoke, where an asm target block has more than one predecessor. In the issue reproducer the asm's fallthrough return block is also the fallthrough successor of the label block, so the output writeback to `%a` is emitted in that shared return block after the label block stores `7`.
cases.inputs: a = 5 (i16), take_label = true and then take_label = false; expected fixed label result 7, wrong label result 5; fallthrough result 5 in both.

cases.summary: Confirmed bug fix in MakeByMoveBody (StateTransform): when the by-move body replaces a child capture of type `&Foo` with an owned by-move capture `Foo` (field remapping has `peel_deref == true`), the pass must also replace a direct fake shallow borrow of that upvar (`_N = &fake shallow (_1.field)`) with `nop`. Leaving/visiting that obsolete fake borrow is the historically incorrect behavior and is associated with the reported ICE `by_move_body.rs:275:21: There should be at least a single deref for an upvar local initialization, found []` (Fixes #138501). Fake borrows that go through a deref, or fields not converted ref->non-ref, are not removed.
cases.trigger: The by-move body contains a `StatementKind::Assign` whose rvalue is `Rvalue::Ref(_, BorrowKind::Fake(FakeBorrowKind::Shallow), place)`, where `place.as_ref()` is `PlaceRef { local: ty::CAPTURE_STRUCT_LOCAL, projection: [ProjectionElem::Field(idx, _)] }` and `self.field_remapping.get(&idx)` is `Some(&(_, _, true, _))` (the `peel_deref` flag is true).
cases.inputs: place=CaptureDirect(0), remap={child_field:0, peel_deref:true}; controls: CaptureDeref(0) with same remap, and CaptureDirect(0) with peel_deref:false

cases.summary: Coverage instrumentation no longer stores a function body span in `FunctionCoverageInfo`. Empty coverage spans are still enlarged to an adjacent `{`/`}` by one ASCII byte, but the expansion is now bounded by source-file access instead of the function body span. File selection for region tables now uses the first coverage mapping's span rather than the body span.
cases.trigger: An empty coverage mapping span is encountered at the function-body boundary, adjacent to `{` or `}`, and the old code's `try_next`/`try_prev` body-span checks would have rejected expansion.
cases.inputs: src = "fn f(){fn g(){}{}}"; body_lo = 13; body_hi = 15; span_lo = 15; span_hi = 15

cases.summary: InstrumentCoverage PR replacing risky span splitting/extension with containment-checked call spans, macro-name truncation, and hole-overlap discarding. It is a span-extraction/refinement robustness refactor, not a reproduced bug report; the only clearly non-semantic optimization is the `pop_front_if` drain helper.
cases.trigger: Compiling with coverage instrumentation when MIR contains a Call/TailCall with a constant callee span, a visible bang-macro invocation span, or any extracted coverage span that overlaps a hole; the old code would then modify/split those spans, while the new code substitutes only contained constant spans, truncates macro spans through `!`, and drops hole-overlapping spans.
cases.inputs: spans = [Span { lo: 0, hi: 100 }]; holes = [Span { lo: 40, hi: 60 }]

cases.summary: Adds a `slice_get_unchecked` intrinsic and teaches `LowerIntrinsics` to lower it to a direct MIR slice projection (`&(*slice_ptr)[index]` / `&mut` / `&raw const` / `&raw mut`), so `<usize as SliceIndex<[T]>>::get`/`get_mut`/`get_unchecked*` stop expanding to thin-pointer casts plus `intrinsics::offset` and instead become one obvious projection statement.
cases.trigger: `LowerIntrinsics` sees a call to `sym::slice_get_unchecked` with exactly two arguments, where the first argument is a non-indirect place (slice reference or raw slice pointer) and the second is a local `usize` place. The lowering constructs a deeper place with `ProjectionElem::Deref` then `ProjectionElem::Index(index_local)` and emits an `Rvalue::RawPtr` or `Rvalue::Ref` chosen from the intrinsic's generic return type.
cases.inputs: data = [10, 20, 30, 40]; raw slice pointer = slice_from_raw_parts(data.as_ptr().add(1), 2); index = 2 (outside metadata but within allocation)

cases.summary: On 32-bit x86 Windows, MSVC fails to align u64/i64 and other >4-byte-aligned types reliably. Historically CheckAlignment was simply disabled for i686-pc-windows-msvc, and alignment was otherwise treated as fully reliable. The fix introduces Target::max_reliable_alignment() (4 bytes for is_like_windows && arch=="x86", otherwise Align::MAX), weakens CheckAlignment's alignment mask to the reliable-alignment mask instead of skipping the pass, and clamps align annotations used by LLVM loads/stores and function-argument pointee alignment.
cases.trigger: Triggered when alignment is requested on 32-bit x86 Windows: `self.is_like_windows && self.arch == "x86"` yields max_reliable_alignment 4. In CheckAlignment, the mask-clamping branch runs when `max_align < Align::MAX`; load/store and pointee-align clamps change behavior only when the requested alignment exceeds the target's reliable alignment.
cases.inputs: addr=4, required_align=8; addr=8, required_align=8; addr=2, required_align=8; addr=4, required_align=4

cases.summary: Bug fix (ICE, not an optimization): `ElaborateDrops` must not assume a failed field-type normalization implies `body.tainted_by_errors` is set. Normalization can fail due to many earlier errors that dropck did not taint, so the pass should recover with an error type and `span_delayed_bug` instead of panicking via `expect`. Regression tests promote two `tests/crashes/*` cases to `tests/ui/drop/drop_elaboration_with_errors{2,3}.rs` with explicit expected diagnostics.
cases.trigger: `try_normalize_erasing_regions` returns `Err(_)` inside `ElaborateDrops` while `body.tainted_by_errors` is `None` because the normalization failure stems from earlier errors not registered by dropck.
cases.inputs: Call with (Ok(7), None), (Err(()), Some(9)), and the triggering input (Err(()), None). The trigger models a field type that fails try_normalize_erasing_regions while body.tainted_by_errors is None.

In those cases the old code emitted a single oversized mapping (or widened the signature mapping) instead of preserving separate spans.

cases.summary: Bug fix in the MIR lint pass `CheckUnnecessaryTransmutes`: an inaccessible source snippet for a `transmute` argument (seen with `--remap-path-prefix`) must skip the optional lint rather than panic via `span_to_snippet(...).expect("ok")`. The regression test uses an auxiliary macro crate whose transmute argument span cannot be snippet-retrieved.
cases.trigger: `CheckUnnecessaryTransmutes` visits a terminator calling the `transmute` intrinsic, and `span_to_snippet(arg)` returns `Err(SourceNotAvailable { ... })`, for example because a span came from an auxiliary crate/macro mapped by `--remap-path-prefix`. Under the historical code, `.expect("ok")` panics while building MIR; under the corrected logic, the `let Ok(snippet)` guard fails and the lint is silently skipped.
cases.inputs: unavailable = Err(SourceNotAvailable); available = Ok("let e = $e; std::mem::transmute(e)")

cases.summary: The CheckUnnecessaryTransmutes MirLint stopped suggesting `(x == 1)` for `u8 -> bool` transmutes because that rewrite is not semantics-preserving: the transmute carries an implicit `assume(u8 < 2)`, while a comparison accepts every u8 and simply returns false for out-of-range values. The lint now intentionally leaves u8 -> bool to clippy.
cases.trigger: A `u8 -> bool` (more generally `Uint(_) -> Bool`) transmute is encountered by CheckUnnecessaryTransmutes and the old arm would have proposed replacing it with `({arg} == 1)`. The suggestion should not fire because the source value is not guaranteed to be 0 or 1.

cases.summary: Bug fix in the `ElaborateDrops` MIR pass: async-drop elaboration read `is_cleanup` from the original body using a block id that could refer to a new block added by `MirPatch`, causing an ICE on partly dropped tuples. The fix uses a shared `MirPatch::block` getter that resolves both original-body and patched block indices, and reuses it in `terminator_loc` and `source_info_for_location`.
cases.trigger: Async-drop elaboration reaches `DropCtxt::build_drop` with a `bb` whose index is at or beyond `body.basic_blocks.len()`, i.e. a block newly appended by `MirPatch`. Directly indexing `body[bb]` then accesses the wrong block/out-of-range data instead of the patched block's `is_cleanup`.
cases.inputs: body.blocks = [{is_cleanup:false}, {is_cleanup:true}], patch.new_blocks = [{is_cleanup:false}], bb = 2 (== body.blocks.len()), is_coroutine = true, allow_async_drops = true, needs_async_drop = true. The original lookup sees the patched block (is_cleanup=false) and yields true. The wrong direct body index is out of range for the original body and panics; the harness catches that deterministic panic and prints code 2.

cases.summary: Coverage metadata must not emit a function whose local file table contains a local file ID with no mapping region, because LLVM asserts on unused local file IDs. The fix detects such functions (via `check_local_file_table` over all coverage spans) and skips their covfun record, and moves empty-span enlargement from LLVM codegen into the InstrumentCoverage MIR span pipeline so spans are non-empty before merge/dedup. Downstream MIR (e.g. CleanupPostBorrowck dumps) sees the enlarged spans.
cases.trigger: A function's coverage `local_file_table` contains at least one local file ID that no `CoverageSpan`/region references (e.g. an injected dummy file entry, or a file whose spans were all dropped), so LLVM's assertion about local file IDs with no mapping regions would fire if the covfun record were emitted.
cases.inputs: injected_unused: local_file_table_len=2, referenced_file_ids=[0]; fully_used: local_file_table_len=2, referenced_file_ids=[0,1]; empty: local_file_table_len=0, referenced_file_ids=[]

cases.summary: A 2024-era Rust PR migrates `TyCtxt::coroutine_layout` and its helpers from `Option` to `Result<_, &LayoutError>`. The important reusable invariant is that failure reasons are now explicit: not-fully-specialized async-drop coroutine arguments yield `LayoutError::TooGeneric`, while a missing raw coroutine layout yields `LayoutError::Unknown`. `Validator` intentionally converts the `Result` back to an option with `.ok()` because layout unavailability is advisory there, preserving its raw-layout fallback behavior.
cases.trigger: Querying the layout of a coroutine whose arguments are not fully specialized, or whose optimized MIR has no raw coroutine layout, while running MIR validation or layout computation.

cases.summary: GVN had to stop simplifying indexed projections of repeated arrays when the index is a non-SSA local and the resulting value cannot be converted to a local. Otherwise simplification could use a later-modified index, which the linked issue calls an incorrect index access and which can introduce an out-of-bounds access.
cases.trigger: GVN processes an indexed projection of a `Value::Repeat` and observes a non-SSA index local. The bail-out path is reached when later simplification cannot turn the projected value into a local (`try_as_local` fails). Concrete shape: `array = [*val; 5]; elem = &array[idx1]; idx1 = idx2; RET = *elem;` with `idx1` non-SSA and modified after `elem` is created.
cases.inputs: idx1 = 0, idx2 = 5, val = 0, matching the regression test's repeat_place(0, 5, &0). The reference is created with idx1 = 0 (in bounds); idx1 is then overwritten with idx2 = 5 before the read. Original reads through the saved reference, while the wrong rewrite indexes the repeated array with 5 and panics.

cases.summary: EarlyOtherwiseBranch was fixed to stop synthesizing StorageLive/StorageDead markers when it hoists a second discriminant comparison. The old code placed StorageDead at statement index 0 of each branch target; when a target was the same block containing the new switchInt (a self-loop), that StorageDead landed before the `switchInt(move _temp)` use, producing a use of a dead local. The fix removes all storage markers for the created temps instead of adding more CFG edges.
cases.trigger: A branch target of the transformed switchInt equals the parent block where the new comparison temp is used, causing the inserted `StorageDead` at `statement_index: 0` of that target to precede the `switchInt(move _temp)`. The issue title is "EarlyOtherwiseBranch can insert storage markers incorrectly, creating use of a dead local"; the reproduction is a `match` whose fallback arm is `_ => bb1` while bb1 is also the block containing the match.
cases.inputs: seed = 19 (entered into the self-looping bb1, where the original match returns 19 while the buggy dead-temp read loops until the observation bound and returns -1)

cases.summary: ElaborateDrops' async-drop lookup blindly took the first associated item of the AsyncDrop trait as the drop function. It must instead require `DefKind::AssocFn` and `check_args_compatible` before constructing the async drop call; otherwise malformed impls (associated type instead of `drop`, or a `drop` with the wrong signature) trigger an ICE instead of normal diagnostics.
cases.trigger: An `impl AsyncDrop for T` provides an associated type in place of the async drop function, or provides an associated function with an incompatible signature, and a `T` value is dropped inside an async function, causing drop elaboration to select that non-drop associated item and construct an async drop call from it.
cases.inputs: Four concrete associated-item slices representing the AsyncDrop trait's associated_item_def_ids: [associated type first, valid drop fn second], [incompatible assoc fn first, valid drop fn second], [valid drop fn first, associated type second], and empty. All items are compile-time constants; no external input.

cases.summary: In the coroutine drop expansion (expand_async_drops), the synthetic yield emitted when an internal async-drop future returns Pending was hard-coded to the boolean constant `false`. That is valid for ordinary gen/return-yield situations but wrong for AsyncGen coroutines, whose yield type is `Poll<Option<T>>`. cases.summary: Historical ReferencePropagation miscompile fix: before this PR the pass ran SSA propagation directly while SsaLocals treated Operand::Move as a read, so a pointer/reference local moved into a call could still be treated as available for reference propagation. The fix preprocesses the body to turn pointer-typed Operand::Move into Operand::Copy before the SSA loop, because Move is pass-by-pointer and the callee may write through/overwrite the moved local. Non-pointer moves are left unchanged.

cases.summary: Confirmed bug fix: async-drop lowering for `StateTransform` (`coroutine/drop.rs`) and `Drop` elaboration must emit `StorageDead` for the pinned future temporary on every control-flow path, including the poll-switch block and the unwind/dropline cleanup blocks. Previously the poll switch was built before the pinned temporary's `Place` existed, so no `StorageDead` was emitted there, and `elaborate_drop` only emitted `StorageDead(fut)` in the success block. This left `StorageLive` without a matching `StorageDead`, corrupting MIR storage-liveness invariants and causing ICEs under `-Zlint-mir`/`-Zvalidate-mir`. The `Inline` pass can expose the bad shape (test `live-dead-storage4` runs `-Zmir-enable-passes=+Inline -Zvalidate-mir -Zlint-mir`).

cases.summary: CopyProp's copy equivalence classes must be formed with borrowedness tracked at the class level, not patched only at replacement time. The historical implementation merged classes without regard to borrowed locals and then skipped replacement of individual borrowed locals during the visit; this could unify two distinct borrowed storages. The fix forbids merging two classes when both already contain a borrowed member, while still allowing a non-borrowed local to join a class that contains a borrowed local.
cases.trigger: A CopyProp input contains a copy/move assignment connecting two locals that are both recorded in `ssa.borrowed_locals()`, directly or because one side is already a class head whose class contains a borrowed member. Equivalently, the class being joined and the class of the source both satisfy `borrowed_classes.contains(...)`.

The PR makes the interning key `(Value, Ty)` and derives projections/casts from the stored type, fixing ICEs in malformed coroutine layouts (#128094) and nonsensical-sized-str bodies (#135128). Regression expectations also change for ZST transmute folding and `PtrMetadata` of thin pointers.

cases.summary: Confirmed bug-fix PR for CopyProp: the guard against unifying borrowed locals only rejected unification when BOTH locals were borrowed (`&&`); the fix rejects unification when EITHER is borrowed (`||`). Merging a borrowed local with a non-borrowed one was unsound because the borrowed local may be written through its reference before the copied value is read again, producing miscompilations (issue #143491). Regression tests pin the conservative behavior by keeping the copy assignments that were previously eliminated.

A later write through the borrow to the borrowed local (for example via a loop-carried reference) then makes the propagated read stale, yielding incorrect behavior.

cases.summary: ElaborateDrops bug fix: clearing a Box's drop flag at the start of its destructor block skipped the allocator's drop because the same flag guards the allocator field. The fix removes the early shallow clear and destructor-only flag test, and instead guards the whole ADT destructor block with one drop-flag test, leaving clearing to the later drop ladder. Adds run-pass and MIR-diff regression tests for conditional Box drops with a dropping allocator.
