cases.summary: The MIR inliner's cycle query (`mir_callgraph_cyclic` in `inline/cycle.rs`) used an `FxHashSet` named `seen` to avoid revisiting instances. That lost the information that an already-visited callee reaches the root, so when a recursive callee was reachable through more than one path, the second path was skipped and the local caller was never added to `involved` as recursive. Two mutually recursive functions could therefore each fail to consider the other a recursion participant, producing a query cycle. Fix: `seen` becomes `FxHashMap<Instance, bool>` caching "reaches root"; direct target hits are inserted as `true`, cached values are propagated on revisits, and `involved` is populated whenever a callee reaches the root.
cases.trigger: A recursive callee is encountered more than once during the cycle DFS: the first visit recurses (possibly discovering that it reaches the root), but the second visit sees the instance already in `seen` and is skipped. If the second occurrence is the one that would have propagated "reaches root" to the current caller, that caller is not added to `involved`. In the fn_traits example, `<{a} as FnOnce>::call_once` recurses into `a` (a cyclical path through a foreign item not marked as a cyclic def id), then `<{b} as FnOnce>::call_once` recurses into `b`; when `b` calls `<{a} as FnOnce>::call_once`, `a` is already in `seen`, so the recursion is not propagated, `b` is not collected as recursive, and similarly in the flipped direction this yields two functions that do not consider each other recursive, causing a query cycle.
cases.inputs: No runtime inputs. Fixed graph from the PR: a -> {call_once(a), call_once(b)}, b -> {call_once(b), call_once(a)}, call_once(a) -> a, call_once(b) -> b; root/target is a (node 0), local nodes are a=0 and b=1.

cases.summary: Bug fix in the SSA copy-class computation feeding CopyProp: the guard against unifying borrowed locals used `&&` (skip only if both are borrowed), so a borrowed local could be unified with a non-borrowed local. The fix uses `||` (skip if either is borrowed). This prevents CopyProp from removing copies into a borrowed local or substituting the other local's value when the borrowed storage may be overwritten before the borrow is read again, as in the added `borrow_in_loop` regression test.
cases.trigger: A copy relation `local = copy rhs` whose representative `head = copies[rhs]` has exactly one endpoint in `borrowed_classes` (one local's address is taken, the other is not). Under the old `&&` guard the two were unified; under the fix they remain distinct. The unsoundness becomes observable when the borrowed local is assigned after the borrow is created and then read through the reference again after a loop backedge.
cases.inputs: No external inputs: check() is called once from main with no arguments.

cases.summary: Historical match lowering produced inconsistent drop/borrow order for pattern bindings under or-patterns. Match arms used the last lowered sub-branch to define arm drop order, and or-pattern bindings were appended after other bindings, so they dropped first instead of at the position of their primary syntactic occurrence. The fix reverses sub-branch lowering so the first source sub-branch supplies drop order, and records or-pattern binding placeholders so bindings are flattened in written order. Knowledge is observed through SimplifyCfg-initial.after-ElaborateDrops MIR diffs; the implementation change itself is in rustc_mir_build match lowering.
cases.trigger: A match arm (or another pattern-matching construct) has an or-pattern whose alternatives bind names in a different order from other bindings, or has bindings inside an or-pattern that would previously have been treated as trailing. Guards make the last-sub-branch behavior especially visible because the old code retained the drop order of the final sub-branch lowered. Example from the regression test: `match (true, LogDrop(o,2), LogDrop(o,1)) { (true, x, y) | (false, y, x) => {} }` was expected to drop `x`, `y` but the corrected behavior is `y`, `x` based on the first alternative.
cases.inputs: entry(true); entry(false)

cases.summary: ImpossiblePredicates must consider the full predicate chain (including parent predicates) and must guard error-carrying and unevaluated-const-projection clauses. The old pass used only the body def's own global predicates, so bodies of nested/derived items under an impossible ancestor bound stayed reachable; later MIR optimization/const-eval then hit uncomputable layouts and ICE'd. The fix also deliberately clears error-referencing bodies, degrading const-eval diagnostics to "entering unreachable code".

Const promotion, array-length evaluation, or GVN simplification then produces an operand/layout inconsistent with the ABI, e.g. "Got a scalar pair where a scalar was expected", "invalid immediate for given destination place: value ScalarPair ... does not match ABI Scalar", or an "unknown layout" ICE.

cases.summary: Bug-fix knowledge for contract lowering: do not merely gate the contract panic at runtime; guard construction/evaluation of contract code itself with the compile-time contract-checks flag. cases.summary: GVN symbolizes values: most `(Value, Ty)` pairs are deduplicated, but `Opaque`, `Address` borrows/pointers, and non-deterministic constants are unique by construction and must never be unified with another value. The historical implementation hashed and equality-checked every such value in an `FxIndexSet` even though a fresh counter guaranteed uniqueness, wasting work. This PR adds a `ValueSet` with `insert_unique` (no hashing, always a fresh `VnIndex`) and a `VnOpaque` marker whose `Hash`/`PartialEq` are `unreachable!()`, so accidentally hashing or comparing a unique value ICEs instead of silently deduplicating it.
cases.trigger: GVN's symbolic execution creates a root value that is intended to be unique: `new_opaque`, address/borrow creation with provenance, insertion of a non-deterministic constant, or invalidation of cached derefs. A deduplicating value set must not hash/merge these; conversely, the ordinary `insert` path must be used for values like deterministic constants that should be unified.
cases.inputs: No external inputs; the harness calls run() with its fixed local sequence.

Instead of unconditionally placing the alwaysinline attribute on the callee definition, codegen now places the inline attribute at the callsite when target features match; otherwise it omits the attribute and the MIR lint warns that the function will not be inlined.
cases.trigger: A direct call or tail call from a caller whose effective target features do not include all target features required by an `#[inline(always)]` callee, while the unstable feature `target_feature_inline_always` is enabled.
cases.inputs: One concrete direct call: callee_inline_always=true, callee_features=0b101, caller_features=0b000. The caller is missing every required feature, so unconditionally placing alwaysinline on the callee definition is unsound. callee_features is non-empty, satisfying the historical `check_result` guard.

cases.summary: GVN's aggregate-to-copy simplification was extended from only LHS locals to LHS places whose projections are all stable offsets. The safe optimization replaces a reconstructed aggregate with a copy from the value-numbered source aggregate, but it must not create an aliasing/overlapping assignment such as `*a = copy (*b)` when the LHS has a deref/non-stable projection, and its regression tests also guard against creating assignments between different fields of the same local.
cases.trigger: GVN simplifies an aggregate: the field list is non-empty, the first field value is a `Value::Projection`, every field is a corresponding `ProjectionElem::Field` from the same aggregate value with matching indices, and `self.ty(copy_from_local_value) == ty`. If `try_as_place` returns a place, GVN rewrites the aggregate to `Rvalue::Use(Operand::Copy(place))` and records `self.reused_locals.insert(place.local)`. This rewrite is only safe when the LHS projection consists entirely of stable offsets.
cases.inputs: victim(Adt::A(7)); victim(Adt::B(9));

cases.summary: GVN's place reconstruction must not append projections after an already-terminal `Deref` when no local has been recovered. Doing so can create an ill-formed MIR place. The fix makes `try_as_place` return `None` in that case; the supplied patch contains only the compiler change, with no regression-test hunk.
cases.trigger: `try_as_place` reaches the `else if projection.last() == Some(&PlaceElem::Deref)` state—i.e. a local was not found and the current projection already ends in `Deref`—while attempting to reconstruct a place through further `Value::Projection` values.
cases.inputs: A fixed GVN value graph: 3 -> Projection(pointer=2, Field(1)); 2 -> Projection(pointer=1, Deref); 1 -> Projection(pointer=0, Field(2)); 0 -> Local(7). reconstruct is called at index 3.

cases.summary: Adding `panic=immediate-abort` requires unwind-sensitive MIR passes to classify the new strategy as non-unwinding even though it is distinct from `Abort`. The PR replaces `== Abort`/`!= Abort` checks in `RemoveNoopLandingPads` and coroutine `StateTransform::can_unwind` with `panic_strategy().unwinds()`, whose only true case is `Unwind`. This is reusable integration knowledge for new panic-strategy variants; it is not evidence of a reproduced optimization bug.
cases.trigger: Compiling code with `-Cpanic=immediate-abort` and running MIR passes whose behavior depends on whether panics unwind, particularly `RemoveNoopLandingPads` and `StateTransform`.
cases.inputs: The concrete panic strategies Unwind, Abort, and ImmediateAbort, each observed three times. The diverging input is ImmediateAbort: corrected `unwinds()` returns false, while the old `!= Abort` predicate returns true.

cases.summary: `AbortUnwindingCalls` gained a `target_supports_unwinding` check so that wasm targets on panic=abort without `exception-handling` treat `UnwindResume` as `Unreachable` and suppress call cleanup landing pads even when the callee ABI is `C-unwind`, preventing LLVM from emitting unsupported EH instructions. Fixes rust-lang/rust#140293.
cases.trigger: A call or `UnwindResume` in MIR whose ABI permits unwinding, on a target that fundamentally cannot unwind (wasm + PanicStrategy::Abort + no `exception-handling` target feature). The issue's reproducer is two `pub extern "C-unwind"` functions where one calls the other, built for wasm32 without `-Ctarget-feature=exception-handling`; `catch_call` appears at opt-level < 2.
cases.inputs: Case 1: is_like_wasm=true, panic_abort=true, exception_handling=false, body_can_unwind=true, call_can_unwind=true, UnwindResume=false, Call=true, initial_unwind_action=Cleanup. Case 2: same target, UnwindResume=true, Call=false, initial_unwind_action=Continue. Case 3 control: is_like_wasm=false, Call=true, initial_unwind_action=Cleanup.

cases.summary: DestinationPropagation's live-interval construction only marked Def/PartialWrite places live in the second half of a statement, so reads inside aggregate rvalues were treated as dead by the statement's twostep. That allowed unification of an aggregate's destination local with a local read by the aggregate, producing self-overlapping aggregate assignments (e.g. a tuple swap rewritten as `_1 = (_1.1, _1.0)`), which clobbers values needed by later fields. The fix marks Use places live through the statement by default, except for simple `_a.stuff = {copy|move} _b.stuff` assignments with identical projections, where marking the rhs local live would block intended unification.
cases.trigger: DestinationPropagation computes a local's live interval as ending before the second half of a statement even though that local is read later within an aggregate assignment, so it unifies the aggregate destination with the read local and creates an overlapping assignment.
cases.inputs: x = 3u8, y = 7u8 (distinct values). Original swap yields (7,3); overlapping aggregate yields (7,7).

cases.summary: ImpossiblePredicates must treat a MIR body tainted by earlier typeck/borrowck errors as "impossible" and replace its body with a single `unreachable`, not only bodies whose elaborated predicates reference errors or are impossible. The PR fixes ICEs caused by later drop elaboration / state transform running over bodies that failed typeck or borrowck, including recursive TAIT/drop-elaboration and coroutine move cases, and changes expected diagnostics for const promotion.
cases.trigger: Run the ImpossiblePredicates MIR pass on a body for which `body.tainted_by_errors.is_some()` is true even though `predicates.references_error() || traits::impossible_predicates(tcx, predicates)` is false. In that situation the pre-fix pass left the failing body intact, and later MIR phases such as drop elaboration or state transform could ICE instead of producing ordinary diagnostics.
cases.inputs: Four concrete deterministic input pairs: (false,false), (false,true), (true,false), (true,true). The distinguishing case is (tainted_by_errors=true, impossible_predicates=false): the old predicate-only transformation leaves BODY_VALUE=42, while the corrected taint-aware transformation clears the body and produces CLEARED=0xDEADBEEF.

cases.summary: JumpThreading replaces its expensive dominator-based loop-header computation with a postorder approximation so it can still avoid threading through loop headers without paying for dominators. The PR is a performance optimization, not a confirmed bug fix, and adds no regression tests.
cases.trigger: JumpThreading must avoid threading through loop headers so it does not create irreducible CFGs, but computing dominators is expensive and "accounts up to 20 % of the runtime of the JumpThreading pass for some cases like serde." The pass therefore needs a cheaper conservative loop-header heuristic.

cases.summary: Make MIR-inliner cycle detection fallible: `mir_callgraph_cyclic` must bail (return `None`) when its call-graph walk exhausts the recursion limit, and the inliner must refuse to inline instead of trusting a partial set of cyclic callees. This is a confirmed fix for rust-lang/rust#146998.
cases.trigger: The recursion limit is encountered while `mir_callgraph_cyclic` walks callees during the inliner's `check_mir_is_available` decision.
cases.inputs: cycle_check(3), cycle_check(6), cycle_check(7) over the fixed chain 0->1->2->3->4->5->6->7->0 with cyclic target 7

cases.summary: GVN processes MIR blocks in reverse postorder while caching dereferenced places. For acyclic CFGs reverse postorder is topological, but with loops a cached deref can be stale at a loop header because a not-yet-processed loop-body terminator may have performed an indirect write. The fix computes `maybe_loop_headers` and calls `state.invalidate_derefs()` when visiting each loop header, preventing GVN from reusing the pre-loop deref value across the back edge. The added mir-opt and run-pass tests exercise an enum mutated through `&mut` inside a loop after its field was copied out before the loop.
cases.trigger: Visiting a loop header in reverse postorder while GVN still has derefs cached from before the loop, when the loop body (not yet processed) contains an indirect write aliasing the cached deref. In the regression program the header is reached again via the back edge after `*val = Value::V1`, so the cached value of `*val_alias` is stale.
cases.inputs: The harness starts with a fresh `Value::V0(1)`. The loop writes `Value::V1` on the first iteration via the same pointer and then returns on the second iteration.

cases.summary: GVN must invalidate cached dereferences at loop headers because reverse postorder is not topological once loops exist; otherwise a cached deref of a reference can be reused across a back-edge even though the loop body performs an indirect write through an aliasing place. The PR fixes the miscompile by calling state.invalidate_derefs() at every maybe-loop-header and adds both a MIR-pass regression test and a -O run-pass regression test.
cases.trigger: A loop whose back-edge/body contains an indirect write through a reference aliasing a place whose dereference GVN has cached, combined with processing the loop header in reverse postorder before that write has been visited. The header is recognized by `loops::maybe_loop_headers`, which inserts a successor into the set when it is not yet visited during postorder traversal, and marks a block visited only after checking its successors to handle self-loops.
cases.inputs: UnsafeCell::new(1i32)

cases.summary: The MIR inliner must compare the complete sanitizer function attributes of caller and callee, not just the disabled-sanitizer bit set. This PR adds LLVM RealtimeSanitizer support, introducing RtsanSetting (Nonblocking/Blocking/Caller) alongside the existing disabled sanitizer set, and consequently widens the inline compatibility gate and the inline(always) warning to the full SanitizerFnAttrs. This is a feature-addition PR, not a confirmed historical bug fix; the reusable invariant concerns inline/force-inline legality.
cases.trigger: The inline pass evaluates a callee whose full sanitizer attributes differ from the caller's while their disabled-sanitizer bit sets are equal, specifically because `rtsan_setting` differs; or a force-inlined function has a non-default sanitize setting such as `realtime = "nonblocking"`.
cases.inputs: Six fixed attribute pairs enumerated in the harness: (disabled=0,Nonblocking|0,Caller), (0,Blocking|0,Nonblocking), (0,Caller|0,Caller), (ADDRESS,Nonblocking|ADDRESS,Blocking), (0,Caller|ADDRESS,Caller), (ADDRESS,Caller|ADDRESS,Caller).

cases.summary: offset_of! lowering changed from a dedicated MIR `Rvalue::NullaryOp(NullOp::OffsetOf(fields), ty)` to a const block that sums calls to a new `offset_of::<T>(variant: u32, field: u32)` intrinsic. Const-prop passes that previously folded the dedicated OffsetOf rvalue must stop handling it; instead the const block is evaluated, folding to a constant only when the container is concrete, while generic containers remain opaque.
cases.trigger: A const block produced by `offset_of!` is encountered by DataflowConstProp/GVN/KnownPanicsLint. If its container type is fully concrete, the block's `offset_of::<T>(variant, field)` calls and additions can be const-evaluated and the whole const block replaced by a concrete `usize`. If the container is generic (e.g. `Gamma<T>` or `Delta<T>`), layout depends on `T` and the const block must not be folded to a constant.
cases.inputs: none: offset_value takes no arguments

cases.summary: `ReifyFnPointer` now carries target `Safety`. MIR consumers must recognize every `ReifyFnPointer(_)` reification: GVN must keep reifications opaque and unmerged, MentionedItems must still collect the reified item, and validation must adapt a safe source signature when the target fn pointer is unsafe. This PR also fixes a separate HIR coercion inference-variable leak by not re-normalizing the target.
cases.trigger: Any reification cast in MIR, especially a safe fn item coerced to `unsafe fn(...)`, or an `if`/`match` LUB combining safe and unsafe fn items that must produce an unsafe fn pointer. GVN triggers when it processes repeated `ReifyFnPointer`/`ClosureFnPointer` casts.
cases.inputs: which = 1

cases.summary: Historical bug fix in `ElaborateDrops`: normalization failure for an ADT field type during open drop elaboration was wrongly converted into an error type plus a `span_delayed_bug`. The fix preserves the original unnormalized field type via `unwrap_or(field_ty)`, enabling polymorphic drop elaboration for rustc-internal consumers. The supplied patch contains no regression test changes.
cases.trigger: `tcx.try_normalize_erasing_regions(self.elaborator.typing_env(), field.ty(tcx, args))` returns `Err` while `ElaborateDrops` is elaborating an open ADT drop.
cases.inputs: raw_field_ty = 7 (a stand-in type id for an unnormalizable projection-bearing field such as Cow/NonZero), normalization = Normalization::Err, modeling try_normalize_erasing_regions returning Err in the ElaborateDrops PostAnalysis typing environment. The harness calls the same function once with these concrete inputs.
